case_name: Tamil Nadu Rural Development Engineers v Secretary to Government Rural Development Department and others
respondent: Secretary to Government Rural Development Department
facts: The members of the Tamil Nadu Rural Development Engineers' Association (Appellants) were initially appointed as 'Overseers' by the then Highways and Rural Works Department and posted exclusively to various Panchayat Unions for executing all the Civil works / Rural works in the Panchayat Unions of Tamil Nadu.

Since they were earlier under the administrative control of the erstwhile Highways and Rural Works Department, they had no proper avenues of promotion especially for the post of Assistant Engineer (for short 'AE') and many of them were languishing in the same post, i.e., as Overseers, for nearly two decades.

By virtue of G.O. Ms. No. 263, Rural Development Department (in short 'RD Department'), dated 27th December, 1996, the Government of Tamil Nadu decided to set up a separate 'Engineering Wing' for the RD Department itself so as to exercise adequate control over various Central and State sponsored Schemes.

By virtue of G.O. Ms. No. 102, RD Department, dated 25th May, 1998, the Government directed that the then Highways and Rural Works Department should cease forthwith from exercising control over the promotions and appointments in the RD Department.
issues: The Constitutional Validity of G.O. Ms. No. 15, dated 25th January, 2000, and G.O. Ms. No. 102, dated 25th May, 1998, was challenged before the Tribunal by a group of individuals and by the Association of Tamil Nadu Engineering Graduates in O.A. Nos. 5338 and 7766 of 2000.

A group of AE - Direct Recruits, on completion of five years of service in the RD Department, filed O.A. Nos. 1068 to 1081 of 2004 before the Tribunal, praying that they be considered for promotion to the post of AEE in the RD Department under Rule 39 of General Rules.
petitioner_arguments: Appellant-Association made representations to the respondent to fix a ratio of 1:1 among AE- direct recruits and AE- Promotees, for promotion to the post of AEE.
The Appellant-Association challenged the common Seniority List in W.P.No.26276 of 2004.
Appellant-Association also filed Writ Petition No. 9460 of 2005 praying for quashing of the rejection letter issued by the Government on 29th December, 2004.
respondent_arguments: The Government vide letter dated 29th December, 2004 rejected the request of the Appellant-Association to fix a ratio of 1:1, on the ground that the promotions of both the categories have to be made on the basis of the date of joining as Assistant Engineer, irrespective of the source.
court_reasoning: The High Court opined that it cannot lightly ignore the specific stand of the Government that the minimum qualifying service of 5 years in the post of AE for promotion to the post of AEE has been prescribed for the reason that the incumbents should acquire the needed practical experience before taking up 'higher responsibilities' so as to achieve administrative efficiency in the Engineering services.
The Appellants cannot claim that the services rendered by them in the Highways Department as Overseers for 20 years be taken into account for promotion in the RD Department.
holding: By this order, the High Court dismissed the Writ Petitions and the Writ Appeal filed by the Appellant-Association.

The Government vide letter dated 29th December, 2004 rejected the request of the Appellant-Association to fix a ratio of 1:1, on the ground that the promotions of both the categories have to be made on the basis of the date of joining as Assistant Engineer, irrespective of the source.
cases_cited: Tamil Nadu Rural Development Engineers v Secretary to Government Rural Development Department
relied on the judgment of Sub- Inspector Rooplal and Another Vs. Lt. Governor through Chief Secretary
